page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A livestock manure holder in a nitrate vulnerable zone may apply up to 170kg per hectare of nitrogen in livestock manure on their holding in each calendar year.
source_paragraphs: You can apply up to 170kg per hectare of nitrogen in livestock manure on your holding in a nitrate vulnerable zone ( NVZ ) in each calendar year.
explanation: The guidance accurately restates the statutory obligation: the 170 kg per hectare per calendar year ceiling on nitrogen from livestock manure applied to a holding. The guidance characterises this as a permission ('may apply up to') rather than a duty ('must not exceed'), but both formulations describe the same quantitative limit without adding to or subtracting from it.
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer must apply between 10 November and 31 December 2025 for a grassland derogation in 2026.
source_paragraphs: You must apply between 10 November and 31 December 2025 for a grassland derogation in 2026.
explanation: The law opens the application window from 1st October, but the guidance starts it on 10 November, narrowing the permitted opening date and imposing a higher bar on farmers (a later start date). This exceeds the statutory floor without contradicting it under rule 3/4.
law_proposition_text: An application for derogation must be submitted between 1st October and 31st December in the calendar year preceding the calendar year to which the application relates.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide their farm name, address, County Parish Holding (CPH) number, and a map showing the location and extent of the land parcels that make up their holding.
source_paragraphs:
When you apply, you must give the:
farm name, address and your County Parish Holding (CPH) number and provide a map showing the location and extent of the land parcels that make up your holding
explanation: Regulation 36(6) requires the application to be in the form and manner published by the Secretary of State but does not itself specify the particular data fields. The guidance enumerates specific items (farm name, address, CPH number, map), which adds requirements beyond what the statutory text states — hence broader than the floor set by the statute.
law_proposition_text: An application for derogation must be made in the form and manner published by the Secretary of State.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the agricultural area and grassland area of their farm in hectares on 1 January of the year for which they are applying.
source_paragraphs: agricultural area and grassland area of your farm in hectares on 1 January of the year for which you are applying
explanation: Regulation 36(1) establishes that an occupier may apply for a derogation where 80% or more of the agricultural area is sown with grass, but does not itself specify what information (agricultural area and grassland area in hectares as at 1 January) must be supplied in the application. The guidance adds a specific data-provision requirement beyond what this clause states, making it broader than the clause without contradicting it.
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding may apply to the Agency for a derogation where 80% or more of the agricultural area of the holding is sown with grass.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the amount of manure nitrogen produced by grazing livestock kept on their farm during the calendar year in kilograms of nitrogen (kgN).
source_paragraphs: amount of manure nitrogen produced by grazing livestock kept on your farm during the calendar year in kilograms of nitrogen ( kgN )

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the amount of manure nitrogen produced by grazing livestock they intend to bring onto or send off their farm during the calendar year (kgN).
source_paragraphs: amount of manure nitrogen produced by grazing livestock you intend to bring onto or send off your farm during the calendar year ( kgN )
explanation: This provision directly requires the occupier to record the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be brought onto the holding during the derogation year, which corresponds to the guidance requirement to provide the amount of manure nitrogen from grazing livestock intended to be brought onto the farm. The guidance adds the specific metric (kgN) and extends to send-off, but the core obligation is reflected here.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be brought on to the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the amount of manure nitrogen produced by grazing livestock they intend to bring onto or send off their farm during the calendar year (kgN).
source_paragraphs: amount of manure nitrogen produced by grazing livestock you intend to bring onto or send off your farm during the calendar year ( kgN )
explanation: This provision requires recording the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be sent off the holding during the derogation year, directly supporting the part of the guidance about manure sent off the farm.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be sent off the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the total amount of manure nitrogen from grazing livestock on their farm during the calendar year (kgN).
source_paragraphs: total amount of manure nitrogen from grazing livestock on your farm during the calendar year ( kgN )

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the amount of manure nitrogen produced by non-grazing livestock on their farm during the calendar year (kgN).
source_paragraphs: amount of manure nitrogen produced by non-grazing livestock on your farm during the calendar year ( kgN )

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the amount of manure nitrogen produced by non-grazing livestock they intend to bring onto or send off their farm during the calendar year (kgN).
source_paragraphs: amount of manure nitrogen produced by non-grazing livestock you intend to bring onto or send off your farm during the calendar year ( kgN )

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: When applying for a derogation, a farmer must provide the total amount of manure nitrogen from non-grazing livestock on their farm during the calendar year (kgN).
source_paragraphs: total amount of manure nitrogen from non-grazing livestock on your farm during the calendar year ( kgN )
explanation: Schedule 3 para 14(2) requires calculating and recording manure nitrogen from livestock as a derogation condition, but the guidance adds the specific restriction to non-grazing livestock and frames this as an application submission requirement, going beyond what the clause states.
law_proposition_text: Having complied with the duty under sub-paragraph (1), the occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure expected to be produced by the livestock on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a derogation application is successful, the farmer must formally agree in writing to the Environment Agency to fulfil the conditions of their derogation.
source_paragraphs: If your application is successful, you must formally agree to fulfil the conditions of your derogation in writing to the EA .
explanation: Regulation 36(4) requires the occupier to send the Agency a written declaration that derogation conditions will be met, or the derogation lapses — this directly underpins the guidance that a successful applicant must formally agree in writing to the Environment Agency to fulfil the conditions.
law_proposition_text: A derogation granted under regulation 36 ceases to have effect unless the occupier to whom the derogation is granted has sent to the Agency a written declaration that the conditions set out in Schedule 3 (the derogation conditions) will be met in relation to the holding.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The 170kg per hectare nitrogen loading limit applies as an average across the whole holding, including manure deposited directly by grazing livestock and what is spread.
source_paragraphs: This includes manure deposited directly by grazing livestock and what you spread. This limit is the loading limit and applies as an average across your holding.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The Environment Agency will refuse a derogation application if the farmer does not meet the eligibility criteria or does not apply within the specified dates.
source_paragraphs: The EA will refuse your application if you do not meet the eligibility criteria or do not apply within the specified dates. If refused, the EA expects you to follow the 170kg nitrogen per hectare limit.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a derogation application is refused, the Environment Agency expects the farmer to follow the 170kg nitrogen per hectare limit.
source_paragraphs: If refused, the EA expects you to follow the 170kg nitrogen per hectare limit.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The Environment Agency is required to carry out a Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) if a farm falls within or is near a European site designated under the Habitats Regulations, or is within the catchment of a European site in unfavourable conservation status due to nutrient pollution.
source_paragraphs: The EA are required to carry out a Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) if your farm falls within or is near a European site designated under the Habitats Regulations or your farm is within the catchment of a European site that is in unfavourable conservation status due to nutrient pollution.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a Habitats Regulations Assessment shows that granting a derogation would have an adverse effect on a European site, the derogation application may be refused.
source_paragraphs: If the HRA shows that granting a derogation would have an adverse effect on a European site your application may be refused.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The Environment Agency may refuse to give a derogation if the farmer had a derogation during a previous year but did not follow all the conditions for that derogation.
source_paragraphs: The EA may also refuse to give you a derogation if you had a derogation during a previous year but did not follow all the conditions for that derogation.
explanation: Rule 1 would normally apply (factual_statement → UNGROUNDED), but the guidance is substantively asserting a regulatory rule about when the Agency may refuse. The law says the Agency 'must refuse' when a prior-year breach is found, but the guidance states it 'may refuse', which is a weaker and positively contradictory statement within the same regulatory framework.
law_proposition_text: The Agency must refuse a derogation application if the occupier has been found in breach of the derogation conditions during the calendar year preceding that to which the application relates.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer may appeal a refused derogation application within 30 days of the refusal, and an independent panel will consider the appeal.
source_paragraphs: You can appeal within 30 days of your application being refused. An independent panel will consider your appeal.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must meet all the conditions of their derogation and follow the rules that apply when using nitrogen fertilisers and storing organic manures in NVZs.
source_paragraphs: You must meet all the conditions of your derogation and follow the rules that apply when using nitrogen fertilisers and storing organic manures in NVZs .
explanation: This provision directly imposes the obligation on occupiers granted a derogation to meet derogation conditions, which is exactly what the guidance states. The additional reference to nitrogen fertiliser and organic manure storage rules reflects the broader NVZ regulatory framework consistently applied to derogation holders.
law_proposition_text: Where the Agency grants a derogation application, the occupier of the designated holding must meet the derogation conditions in relation to that holding.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a farmer does not meet the conditions of a derogation for the year it covers, the Environment Agency may fine them.
source_paragraphs:
If you do not meet the conditions of a derogation for the year it covers:
the EA may fine you

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a farmer does not meet the conditions of a derogation for the year it covers, they may not be eligible to apply for a derogation in the following year.
source_paragraphs:
If you do not meet the conditions of a derogation for the year it covers:
you may not be eligible to apply for a derogation in the following year

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer will not be allowed to apply more than 170kg of nitrogen per hectare in livestock manure, averaged across their holding, if the Environment Agency withdraws their derogation.
source_paragraphs:
You will not be allowed to apply more than 170kg of nitrogen per hectare in livestock manure, averaged across your holding, if the EA either:
withdraws your derogation
decides you're ineligible to apply for a derogation the following year
explanation: Regulation 7(1) directly imposes the 170kg nitrogen per hectare limit in livestock manure across the holding, which is exactly what the guidance states applies when a derogation is withdrawn. The guidance accurately restates the statutory floor in this provision.
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer may operate under a derogation to use up to 250kg of nitrogen per hectare from grazing livestock manure under certain conditions.
source_paragraphs: You may be able to operate under a derogation to use up to 250kg of nitrogen per hectare from grazing livestock manure under certain conditions.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer will not be allowed to apply more than 170kg of nitrogen per hectare in livestock manure, averaged across their holding, if the Environment Agency decides they are ineligible to apply for a derogation the following year.
source_paragraphs:
You will not be allowed to apply more than 170kg of nitrogen per hectare in livestock manure, averaged across your holding, if the EA either:
withdraws your derogation
decides you're ineligible to apply for a derogation the following year
explanation: Regulation 7(1) imposes the 170 kg/ha livestock-manure nitrogen limit across the holding, which is precisely the rule the guidance states applies when a derogation is unavailable; the guidance accurately reflects this statutory minimum.
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a derogation holder ploughs grassland, they must plant a crop with a high nitrogen demand (for example, grass, potatoes, sugar beet, maize) within 4 weeks from the date of ploughing.
source_paragraphs:
If you plough grassland where you have a derogation, you must plant one of the following:
a crop with a high nitrogen demand (for example, grass, potatoes, sugar beet, maize) within 4 weeks from the date of ploughing
grass within 6 weeks from the date of ploughing
explanation: The guidance accurately restates the statutory requirement in schedule 3, paragraph 10(1)(a): ploughed grassland must be re-sown with a high nitrogen demand crop within four weeks. The examples given (grass, potatoes, sugar beet, maize) are illustrative and consistent with the concept of high nitrogen demand crops.
law_proposition_text: Where any grass on the holding is ploughed, the land must be sown with a crop with high nitrogen demand within four weeks beginning with the day after the ploughing.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a derogation holder ploughs grassland, they must plant grass within 6 weeks from the date of ploughing.
source_paragraphs:
If you plough grassland where you have a derogation, you must plant one of the following:
a crop with a high nitrogen demand (for example, grass, potatoes, sugar beet, maize) within 4 weeks from the date of ploughing
grass within 6 weeks from the date of ploughing
explanation: The law requires sowing with grass within six weeks beginning with the day after ploughing, and the guidance states planting grass within 6 weeks from the date of ploughing. The minor phrasing difference ('day after ploughing' vs 'date of ploughing') is negligible in practical effect, and the substance accurately reflects the legal requirement.
law_proposition_text: Where any grass on the holding is ploughed, the land must be sown with grass within six weeks beginning with the day after the ploughing.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must not plough temporary grassland on sandy soils between 1 July and 31 December.
source_paragraphs: You must not plough temporary grassland on sandy soils between 1 July and 31 December.
explanation: The guidance accurately restates the legal prohibition: temporary grassland on sandy soils must not be ploughed between 1 July and 31 December, matching the candidate clause exactly.
law_proposition_text: Any temporary grassland on sandy soils on the holding must not be ploughed between 1 July and the following 31 December.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must not plough any area of grass before 16 January if they spread livestock manure on that area in the previous year between 1 September and 31 December on sandy soils.
source_paragraphs:
You must not plough any area of grass before 16 January if you've spread livestock manure on that area in the previous year between:
1 September and 31 December on sandy soils
15 October and 15 January on all other soils
explanation: The guidance accurately restates this provision word-for-word in substance: spreading on sandy soils between 1 September and 31 December triggers a prohibition on ploughing before the following 16 January. The guidance adds 'derogation holder' as subject, which is consistent with the derogation scheme context.
law_proposition_text: Where livestock manure has been spread on grass on sandy soils on the holding between 1 September and 31 December, the grass must not be ploughed before the following 16 January.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must not plough any area of grass before 16 January if they spread livestock manure on that area in the previous year between 15 October and 15 January on all other soils.
source_paragraphs:
You must not plough any area of grass before 16 January if you've spread livestock manure on that area in the previous year between:
1 September and 31 December on sandy soils
15 October and 15 January on all other soils
explanation: The guidance accurately restates this provision: livestock manure spread on grass (not on sandy soils) between 15 October and 15 January means no ploughing before the following 16 January. The guidance's phrase 'all other soils' correctly maps to 'not on sandy soils'.
law_proposition_text: Where livestock manure has been spread on grass not on sandy soils on the holding between 15 October and the following 15 January, the grass must not be ploughed before the following 16 January.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must not grow leguminous or other atmospheric nitrogen-fixing plants in their rotation, except grass with less than 50% clover or legumes under-sown with grass.
source_paragraphs:
You must not grow leguminous or other atmospheric nitrogen-fixing plants in your rotation, except:
grass with less than 50% clover
legumes under-sown with grass
explanation: This sub-paragraph provides the second exception (leguminous plants under-sown with grass), which directly corresponds to the 'legumes under-sown with grass' element of the guidance; the guidance accurately restates this provision.
law_proposition_text: Crop rotation on the holding must not include leguminous or other plants fixing atmospheric nitrogen except for— any other leguminous plant that is under-sown with grass.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must not grow leguminous or other atmospheric nitrogen-fixing plants in their rotation, except grass with less than 50% clover or legumes under-sown with grass.
source_paragraphs:
You must not grow leguminous or other atmospheric nitrogen-fixing plants in your rotation, except:
grass with less than 50% clover
legumes under-sown with grass
explanation: This sub-paragraph covers the prohibition and the grass/clover exception, which the guidance reflects accurately, but the guidance also incorporates the second exception (under-sown with grass) from the sibling sub-paragraph — meaning taken alone, this clause only partially grounds the full guidance statement.
law_proposition_text: Crop rotation on the holding must not include leguminous or other plants fixing atmospheric nitrogen, except where the leguminous plant is grass containing less than 50% clover.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must plan the amount of phosphate fertiliser they put on their land in an NVZ.
source_paragraphs: You must plan the amount of phosphate fertiliser you put on your land in an NVZ .
explanation: This provision directly requires the derogation holder to calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser to be spread on the crop, which corresponds to the guidance obligation to plan the amount of phosphate fertiliser put on their land in an NVZ.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of available phosphorus calculated under paragraph (a).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field where a crop is to be planted or has been planted, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate in the soil likely to be available for the crop during the growing season.
source_paragraphs:
You must take the following steps before you use phosphate for the first time in a field where you're going to plant a crop or have planted a crop:
Calculate the amount of phosphate in the soil that's likely to be available for the crop to use during the growing season.
explanation: This clause directly requires the occupier to calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil likely to be available for crop uptake during the growing season, which matches the guidance's description of the obligation to calculate available phosphate before use in a field.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field where a crop is to be planted or has been planted, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate in the soil likely to be available for the crop during the growing season.
source_paragraphs:
You must take the following steps before you use phosphate for the first time in a field where you're going to plant a crop or have planted a crop:
Calculate the amount of phosphate in the soil that's likely to be available for the crop to use during the growing season.
explanation: This is an identical provision to bcand:08f7916de240864d and equally grounds the guidance on the calculation obligation.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.
source_paragraphs: Calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.
explanation: The law requires calculating the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser taking into account available phosphorus, which directly corresponds to the guidance's instruction to calculate the amount of phosphate to get the best crops, accounting for phosphate already in the soil. The guidance accurately reflects this statutory obligation.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of available phosphorus calculated under paragraph (a).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.
source_paragraphs: Calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.
explanation: This clause requires the fertilisation plan to record both the calculated soil phosphorus amount and the optimum phosphate fertiliser amount, effectively confirming that both the calculation of available soil phosphorus and the optimum application calculation are statutory requirements. The guidance reflects these underlying substantive obligations, though bcand:3559c670248ac958 is a more direct anchor.
law_proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must record the amount of phosphorus calculated under paragraph 3(1)(a) and the method used to calculate that figure, and the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop taking into account that phosphorus amount.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.
source_paragraphs: Calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.
explanation: This clause is one part of the two-step calculation process: first calculate available soil phosphorus, then calculate optimum phosphate fertiliser. The guidance conflates both steps into one, so it reflects this clause but incompletely separates the two statutory steps. However, bcand:3559c670248ac958 (item b) is the better anchor as the guidance is specifically about the optimum calculation.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate that should be applied to the crop to get the best crops, taking into account the phosphate already available in the soil.

explanation: Identical in text to bcand:08f7916de240864d; same reasoning applies — this is step (a) of the calculation, and the guidance addresses both steps together without fully distinguishing the first step from the second.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer may apply for a grassland derogation to use up to 250kg of nitrogen per hectare if the nitrogen comes from grazing livestock manure.
source_paragraphs: You can apply for a grassland derogation to use a higher limit of up to 250kg of nitrogen per hectare, if the nitrogen comes from grazing livestock manure.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of phosphate from any planned applications of organic manure that is likely to be available to the crop in the growing season in which it is spread.
source_paragraphs: Calculate the amount of phosphate from any planned applications of organic manure that's likely to be available to the crop in the growing season in which you spread it.
explanation: The law requires all occupiers to record phosphate from organic manure before spreading (no 'first-time use' restriction), whereas the guidance restricts the obligation to derogation holders using phosphate for the first time in a field — a narrower but also differently framed requirement. The guidance also frames this as a calculation step rather than a recording step, and adds the 'first use in a field' qualifier not present in the law, making it broader in specificity relative to a general ob
law_proposition_text: Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied from the organic manure intended to be spread for the purpose of fertilising the crop in the growing season in which it is spread.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using phosphate for the first time in a field, a derogation holder must calculate the amount of manufactured phosphate fertiliser they will need.
source_paragraphs: Calculate the amount of manufactured phosphate fertiliser you will need.
explanation: The law requires the occupier (not specifically a 'derogation holder') to calculate the optimum phosphate amount before spreading, with no restriction to 'first time in a field'. The guidance narrows the obligation to derogation holders and to first-time use in a field, which adds a condition not present in the law clause, making it broader in one sense and narrower in another; on balance the guidance imposes a higher/more specific bar than the statutory text.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of available phosphorus calculated under paragraph (a).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must carry out phosphate availability from organic manure and manufactured phosphate calculations every time they spread manure or fertiliser.
source_paragraphs: You must also carry out steps 3 and 4 every time you spread manure or fertiliser.
explanation: This clause requires recording before spreading organic manure the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied for fertilising the crop in the growing season — this is substantively a phosphate availability calculation per spreading event, aligning with the guidance's description.
law_proposition_text: Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied from the organic manure intended to be spread for the purpose of fertilising the crop in the growing season in which it is spread.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must carry out phosphate availability from organic manure and manufactured phosphate calculations every time they spread manure or fertiliser.
source_paragraphs: You must also carry out steps 3 and 4 every time you spread manure or fertiliser.
explanation: This clause requires recording the amount of manufactured phosphate fertiliser required before spreading — a pre-spread recording obligation. The guidance characterises this as a 'calculation every time they spread', which broadly aligns but conflates recording with calculation and applies it more generally than this specific clause.
law_proposition_text: Before spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the occupier must record the amount required, being the optimum amount of phosphate required by the crop less the amount of phosphate that will be supplied for crop uptake from any organic manure spread.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must carry out phosphate availability from organic manure and manufactured phosphate calculations every time they spread manure or fertiliser.
source_paragraphs: You must also carry out steps 3 and 4 every time you spread manure or fertiliser.
explanation: This clause requires recording total phosphate content of organic manure before spreading, which is one component of the guidance's described obligation. The guidance generalises this into a broader 'phosphate availability calculation' requirement, going beyond mere recording of total content.
law_proposition_text: Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the total phosphate content of the organic manure.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must carry out phosphate availability from organic manure and manufactured phosphate calculations every time they spread manure or fertiliser.
source_paragraphs: You must also carry out steps 3 and 4 every time you spread manure or fertiliser.
explanation: This clause requires calculating the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser taking into account available phosphorus, which is the closest match to a phosphate availability calculation. The guidance is broader in that it states this must happen 'every time they spread manure or fertiliser', while this clause applies to fertiliser planning rather than explicitly requiring repetition per spreading event.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of available phosphorus calculated under paragraph (a).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using manure or fertiliser on any crop (including grass) in following growing seasons, a derogation holder must repeat the calculations for phosphate in the soil and the amount that should be applied.
source_paragraphs:
Before you use manure or fertiliser on any crop (including grass) in following growing seasons, you must:
repeat steps 1 and 2
plan your fertiliser use for that growing season
explanation: This clause requires the occupier to calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser to spread on the crop, accounting for available phosphorus — directly corresponding to the phosphate calculation the guidance requires before use. However, it captures only part of the annual timing element.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of available phosphorus calculated under paragraph (a).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using manure or fertiliser on any crop (including grass) in following growing seasons, a derogation holder must repeat the calculations for phosphate in the soil and the amount that should be applied.
source_paragraphs:
Before you use manure or fertiliser on any crop (including grass) in following growing seasons, you must:
repeat steps 1 and 2
plan your fertiliser use for that growing season
explanation: This clause explicitly requires the phosphate calculation duties (under sub-paragraph 1, including the optimum phosphate amount) to be performed each calendar year before spreading on permanent grassland — directly grounding the guidance's requirement to repeat calculations each growing season.
law_proposition_text: In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the duties under sub-paragraph (1) in each calendar year before spreading phosphate fertiliser.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Before using manure or fertiliser on any crop (including grass) in following growing seasons, a derogation holder must plan their fertiliser use for that growing season.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: For permanent grassland, phosphate calculations must be made based on the farming year starting on 1 January.
source_paragraphs: For permanent grassland, make your calculations based on the farming year starting on 1 January.
explanation: The law requires the occupier of permanent grassland to comply with phosphate-related duties in each calendar year (i.e. starting 1 January) before spreading phosphate fertiliser, which accurately underpins the guidance that phosphate calculations for permanent grassland must be based on the farming year starting 1 January.
law_proposition_text: In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the duties under sub-paragraph (1) in each calendar year before spreading phosphate fertiliser.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must sample and analyse the soil at least once every 4 years to determine the amount of phosphorus available to crops during the growing season.
source_paragraphs: You must sample and analyse the soil at least once every 4 years. This will tell you the amount of phosphorus in the soil that's likely to be available for the crop to use during the growing season.
explanation: The neighbouring proposition explicitly states the five-hectare granularity requirement and the same cropping and soil type qualifier, resolving both specific omissions identified in the original verdict.
law_proposition_text: At least every four years, the occupier of a derogated holding must undertake soil sampling and analysis for the supply of phosphorus of at least every five hectares of the agricultural area under the same cropping regime and soil type.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must carry out soil sampling and analysis for at least every 5 hectares of their holding that has the same cropping and soil type.
source_paragraphs: You must do this for at least every 5 hectares of your holding that has the same cropping and soil type.
explanation: The surrounding guidance explicitly states 'A derogation holder must sample and analyse the soil at least once every 4 years to determine the amount of phosphorus available to crops during the growing season,' which directly covers both the four-yearly periodicity and the phosphorus-specific purpose that the original verdict found missing.
law_proposition_text: At least every four years, the occupier of a derogated holding must undertake soil sampling and analysis for the supply of phosphorus of at least every five hectares of the agricultural area under the same cropping regime and soil type.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder may use existing soil sampling results if they are less than 4 years old when the derogation starts.
source_paragraphs: You can use existing soil sampling results if they're less than 4 years old when your derogation starts.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a derogation holder does not have soil sampling data that is less than 4 years old, they must sample 75% of their farm area in the first year of the derogation.
source_paragraphs: If you have not got sampling data that's less than 4 years old, you'll need to sample 75% of your farm area in the first year of your derogation. You then need to sample the remaining 25% of your farm area in the year of your next derogation.
explanation: The guidance accurately restates the legal requirement: where soil sampling data is not less than 4 years old (i.e., not carried out within four years before grant), 75% of the agricultural area must be sampled, and the guidance's 'first year of the derogation' corresponds to 'no later than 12 months after the grant of the derogation'.
law_proposition_text: Where phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type has not been carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation, such sampling and analysis must be carried out on 75% of the agricultural area no later than 12 months after the grant of the derogation.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: Grazing livestock for the purposes of the grassland derogation are: cattle (except veal calves), sheep, deer, goats, and horses.
source_paragraphs:
Grazing livestock are:
cattle (except for veal calves)
sheep
deer
goats
horses

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must sample the remaining 25% of their farm area in the year of their next derogation if they sampled 75% in the first year.
source_paragraphs: You then need to sample the remaining 25% of your farm area in the year of your next derogation.
explanation: This clause requires 100% sampling by 12 months after the next derogation is granted, meaning the remaining 25% (after 75% was done in year one) must be completed in the year of the next derogation — accurately reflecting the guidance's statement.
law_proposition_text: Where phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type has not been carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation, such sampling and analysis must be carried out on 100% of the agricultural area no later than 12 months after the date on which a derogation is next granted to the occupier.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must sample the remaining 25% of their farm area in the year of their next derogation if they sampled 75% in the first year.
source_paragraphs: You then need to sample the remaining 25% of your farm area in the year of your next derogation.
explanation: This clause governs the first-year 75% sampling obligation (within 12 months of the grant of the derogation), which the guidance presupposes but does not restate. The guidance addresses only the follow-on obligation for the remaining 25%, so this clause is only partially reflected.
law_proposition_text: Where phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type has not been carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation, such sampling and analysis must be carried out on 75% of the agricultural area no later than 12 months after the grant of the derogation.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must record their nitrogen use and any phosphate they use from manufactured fertilisers and organic manures in their fertilisation plan and field records.
source_paragraphs:
In your fertilisation plan and field records you must record your nitrogen use and any phosphate you use from:
manufactured fertilisers
organic manures
explanation: This Schedule 3 derogation condition requires the occupier (derogation holder) to calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure produced by livestock, which partially supports the guidance's claim that derogation holders must record nitrogen and phosphate use from organic manures.
law_proposition_text: Having complied with the duty under sub-paragraph (1), the occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure expected to be produced by the livestock on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must record their nitrogen use and any phosphate they use from manufactured fertilisers and organic manures in their fertilisation plan and field records.
source_paragraphs:
In your fertilisation plan and field records you must record your nitrogen use and any phosphate you use from:
manufactured fertilisers
organic manures
explanation: This is a scope/heading clause that identifies Schedule 3 as the derogation conditions under Regulation 36(4). The guidance goes beyond merely restating this scope by specifying substantive recording obligations, so it is broader than what this clause alone states.
law_proposition_text: A derogation from the nitrate action programme requirements is subject to the conditions set out in Schedule 3, as provided under Regulation 36(4).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must record their nitrogen use and any phosphate they use from manufactured fertilisers and organic manures in their fertilisation plan and field records.
source_paragraphs:
In your fertilisation plan and field records you must record your nitrogen use and any phosphate you use from:
manufactured fertilisers
organic manures
explanation: This clause under Schedule 3 (derogation conditions) specifically requires derogation holders to record phosphate supplied for crop uptake from organic manure within one week of spreading. The guidance mentions phosphate from organic manures but does not specify the one-week deadline, making it incomplete relative to this specific requirement.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must record, within one week of spreading organic manure, the amount of phosphate that was supplied for uptake by the crop.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must record their nitrogen use and any phosphate they use from manufactured fertilisers and organic manures in their fertilisation plan and field records.
source_paragraphs:
In your fertilisation plan and field records you must record your nitrogen use and any phosphate you use from:
manufactured fertilisers
organic manures
explanation: This Schedule 3 derogation condition requires the occupier to record the total phosphorus content within one week of spreading organic manure. The guidance refers to phosphate recording but does not capture this specific timing requirement, making it incomplete.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must record, within one week of spreading organic manure, the total phosphorus content.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must record how much phosphate and nitrogen any manure contains within one week of bringing it onto their holding.
source_paragraphs: You must record how much phosphate and nitrogen any manure contains within one week of bringing it onto your holding.
explanation: Both sit within the same nitrates/manure regulatory framework and address recording nitrogen content of manure brought onto a holding within one week, but the law only requires recording when the nitrogen content is 'not known' and after it is ascertained — whereas the guidance states it must be recorded within one week of bringing the manure onto the holding regardless of prior knowledge. These are substantively inconsistent trigger conditions within the same framework.
law_proposition_text: Where the nitrogen content of livestock manure brought on to a holding is not known, the occupier must record it within one week of ascertaining it.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a derogation holder does not know the phosphate content of manure brought onto their farm, they must analyse or calculate the amount and record it within a week of finding it out.
source_paragraphs: If you do not know the phosphate content of manure you bring onto your farm, you must analyse or calculate the amount. Record the amount within a week of finding it out.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded the size of the agricultural area of their holding in hectares (updated within one month if it changes).
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
the size of the agricultural area of your holding in hectares (update within one month if this changes)
explanation: The law requires recording the total agricultural area and grass area by 1st March each calendar year, which matches the guidance's 1 March deadline; however, the guidance adds a requirement to update within one month if the area changes, which goes beyond what this clause states, making the guidance broader.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must record the total agricultural area and the area of grass within the holding by 1st March for each calendar year.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded the size of the area of grassland for that calendar year in hectares (updated within one month if it changes).
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
the size of the area of grassland for that calendar year in hectares (update within one month if this changes)
explanation: The law requires recording total agricultural area and grass area by 1 March; the guidance specifies the unit (hectares) and adds a requirement to update the record within one month if the area changes, which goes beyond what the statutory text states.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must record the total agricultural area and the area of grass within the holding by 1st March for each calendar year.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded a written description of the livestock housing and manure storage systems on their farm, including the volume of manure storage available.
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
a written description of the livestock housing and manure storage systems you have on your farm, including the volume of the manure storage available
explanation: The law clause requires the occupier to record a description of livestock housing and manure storage systems including volume of storage by 1 March each calendar year, which matches the guidance accurately. The guidance's limitation to derogation years does not conflict — it may simply be contextualising the applicable years without contradicting the legal text.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must make a record describing the livestock housing and manure storage systems together with the volume of manure storage in place on the holding by 1st March for each calendar year.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded the numbers and type of livestock they expect to have on their holding during the remaining part of the calendar year.
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
the numbers and type of livestock you expect to have on your holding during the remaining part of the calendar year
explanation: Paragraph 14(3) sets the 1 March deadline for records required under paragraph 14, directly corroborating the timing element of the guidance. Taken together with paragraph 14(1), this fully supports the guidance.
law_proposition_text: A record required under paragraph 14 must be made by 1st March for the calendar year concerned.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded the numbers and type of livestock they expect to have on their holding during the remaining part of the calendar year.
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
the numbers and type of livestock you expect to have on your holding during the remaining part of the calendar year
explanation: Paragraph 14(1) precisely requires recording the expected number and category (type) of livestock on the holding during the derogation year, matching the substantive content of the guidance. The guidance accurately restates this obligation.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must make a record of the expected number of livestock animals to be kept on the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates, and the category for each animal by reference to the categories in Schedule 1.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded an estimate of the manure nitrogen and phosphate that their livestock will produce during the current calendar year.
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
an estimate of the manure nitrogen and phosphate that your livestock will produce during the current calendar year
explanation: This provision directly requires the occupier to calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure expected to be produced by livestock on the holding during the year, which matches the substance of the guidance (an estimate of manure nitrogen and phosphate from livestock).
law_proposition_text: Having complied with the duty under sub-paragraph (1), the occupier must calculate and record the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in manure expected to be produced by the livestock on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: By 1 March of each year in which a farmer has a derogation, they must have recorded an estimate of the manure nitrogen and phosphate that their livestock will produce during the current calendar year.
source_paragraphs:
By 1 March of each year in which you have a derogation, you must have the following information recorded:
an estimate of the manure nitrogen and phosphate that your livestock will produce during the current calendar year
explanation: This provision establishes the 1 March deadline for the record required under paragraph 14, directly supporting the guidance's statement that the record must be made by 1 March of each year in which the farmer has a derogation.
law_proposition_text: A record required under paragraph 14 must be made by 1st March for the calendar year concerned.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder must send the Environment Agency details about their farming practices and fertiliser use for the period 1 January to 31 December by 30 April in the year following the derogation.
source_paragraphs: You must send the EA details about your farming practices and fertiliser use for the period 1 January to 31 December. You must send the details by 30 April in the year following the derogation. This is your fertilisation account.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer cannot obtain permission to use more than 170kg of nitrogen per hectare from non-grazing livestock (veal calves, pigs, or poultry) and must keep within the 170kg per hectare limit for such livestock.
source_paragraphs: You cannot get permission to use more nitrogen from non-grazing livestock (veal calves, pigs or poultry) and must keep within the 170kg per hectare limit.
explanation: The surrounding guidance explicitly states that 'A livestock manure holder in a nitrate vulnerable zone may apply up to 170kg per hectare of nitrogen in livestock manure on their holding in each calendar year' and that 'The 170kg per hectare nitrogen loading limit applies as an average across the whole holding, including manure deposited directly by grazing livestock and what is spread', thereby c
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A derogation holder's fertilisation account must show the total agricultural area of their derogated holding and the area in hectares covered by specified crops including winter wheat, spring wheat, winter barley, spring barley, winter oilseed rape, sugar beet, potatoes, forage maize, and grass.
source_paragraphs:
Your fertilisation account must show the total agricultural area of your derogated holding and the area (in hectares) covered by each of the following crops:
winter wheat
spring wheat
winter barley
spring barley
winter oilseed rape
sugar beet
potatoes
forage maize
grass
explanation: Neighbouring propositions explicitly cover both omissions: 'other crops' is addressed in the fertilisation account proposition, and the number and category of livestock requirement is covered by the fertilisation plan proposition about livestock numbers and categories.
law_proposition_text: The accounts must record the total agricultural area of the holding, the area covered by each specified crop type (winter wheat, spring wheat, winter barley, spring barley, winter oilseed rape, sugar beet, potatoes, forage maize, grass, and other crops), and the number and category of animals kept on the holding by reference to Schedule 1.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The fertilisation account must show the area covered by other crops (for example, vegetables, lucerne, flowers), but the specific crop does not need to be named.
source_paragraphs: You need to show the area covered by other crops (for example, vegetables, lucerne, flowers), but the specific crop does not need to be named.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must show the number and category of livestock kept on the farm and the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in the manure they produce.
source_paragraphs:
Your fertilisation plan must also show the:
number and category of livestock kept on your farm, and the amount of nitrogen and phosphate in the manure they produce (according to the categories in the standard values tables ( 128 KB ) )

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must show the amount and type of livestock manure brought on or sent off the farm, together with the total amount of nitrogen and phosphate in that manure.
source_paragraphs: amount and type of livestock manure brought on or sent off your farm, together with the total amount of nitrogen and phosphate in that manure

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The fertilisation plan must show the weight in tonnes and nitrogen content of all manufactured nitrogen fertiliser stocks kept on, brought in, or sent off the farm during the calendar year.
source_paragraphs: weight in tonnes and nitrogen content of all manufactured nitrogen fertiliser stocks kept on, brought in or sent off your farm during the calendar year

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The Environment Agency may inspect a derogation holder's farm to make sure they are meeting the conditions of their derogation.
source_paragraphs: The EA may inspect your farm to make sure you're meeting conditions of your derogation.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer whose derogation application is successful must comply with the conditions of the derogation and the NVZ rules.
source_paragraphs: You must comply with the conditions of a derogation and the NVZ rules if your application is successful.
explanation: This Schedule 3 heading (read with Regulation 36(4)) is the direct legal basis for the rule that a derogation is subject to conditions, accurately reflected by the guidance's statement that a successful applicant must comply with the derogation conditions and NVZ rules.
law_proposition_text: A derogation from the nitrate action programme requirements is subject to the conditions set out in Schedule 3, as provided under Regulation 36(4).

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer whose derogation application is successful must comply with the conditions of the derogation and the NVZ rules.
source_paragraphs: You must comply with the conditions of a derogation and the NVZ rules if your application is successful.
explanation: This clause sets out one specific derogation condition (maintaining ≥80% grass cover). The guidance says farmers must comply with all derogation conditions but does not spell out this specific requirement, so the guidance is incomplete relative to this particular mandatory condition.
law_proposition_text: The occupier must maintain the holding to ensure that at least 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass during the calendar year to which the derogation applies.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer whose derogation application is successful must comply with the conditions of the derogation and the NVZ rules.
source_paragraphs: You must comply with the conditions of a derogation and the NVZ rules if your application is successful.
explanation: This clause specifies that a derogation ceases to have effect unless the occupier sends a written declaration to the Agency that Schedule 3 conditions will be met — a specific procedural compliance step. The guidance refers only to complying with conditions generally and omits this written-declaration requirement.
law_proposition_text: A derogation granted under regulation 36 ceases to have effect unless the occupier to whom the derogation is granted has sent to the Agency a written declaration that the conditions set out in Schedule 3 (the derogation conditions) will be met in relation to the holding.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer may only apply for a grassland derogation if at least 80% of the agricultural area of their holding is grass.
source_paragraphs: You can only apply for a derogation if at least 80% of the agricultural area of your holding is grass.
explanation: Regulation 36(1) states that an occupier may apply for a derogation where 80% or more of the agricultural area is sown with grass, which precisely matches the guidance's statement about the 80% grass eligibility condition for applying.
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding may apply to the Agency for a derogation where 80% or more of the agricultural area of the holding is sown with grass.

page_title: Grassland derogations for livestock manure in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: The agricultural area is the part of a holding used for agricultural purposes and does not include surface waters, areas of hardstanding, buildings or woodland (unless woodland is used for grazing), or any land covered by a greenhouse.
source_paragraphs:
The agricultural area is the part of your holding you use for agricultural purposes. It does not include, for example:
surface waters
areas of hardstanding
buildings or woodland (unless the woodland is used for grazing)
any land covered by a greenhouse
explanation: The law proposition provided is blank/empty, meaning there is no actual legal text to conflict with or be incomplete against; the verdict cannot stand without a law proposition to compare the guidance against.
law_proposition_text: The reference to 'agricultural area' in paragraph (1) does not include any land covered by a greenhouse.

page_title: Storing silage, slurry and agricultural fuel oil
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer must follow the rules for storing silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.
source_paragraphs: You must follow these rules if you store silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.
explanation: The surrounding guidance extensively covers the specific procedural notification requirement (14 days' notice before construction) and the broader storage rules, meaning the guidance as a whole is not incomplete with respect to the law proposition's notice obligation.
law_proposition_text: A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil to be kept in a new or improved store must give the Agency notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location at least 14 days before work constructing the new or improved store is to be begun.
law_name: The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010

page_title: Storing silage, slurry and agricultural fuel oil
guidance_proposition_text: The Environment Agency may at any time serve a notice requiring a farmer to bring storage up to current standards if it believes there is a significant risk of pollution.
source_paragraphs: The Environment Agency can also serve a notice at any time requiring you to bring storage up to the current standards if it believes there's a significant risk of pollution.
explanation: Regulation 7(2) describes the standard the Agency must apply when specifying required works — reducing to a minimum any significant risk of pollution — which supports the guidance's framing that notices are issued where there is a significant risk of pollution. However, it is a supplementary provision to reg 7(1) rather than the primary anchor.
law_proposition_text: The works, precautions or other steps required by a notice must be, in the opinion of the Agency, appropriate for reducing to a minimum any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters, having regard to the requirements of the Regulations.
law_name: The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010

page_title: Storing silage, slurry and agricultural fuel oil
guidance_proposition_text: The Environment Agency may at any time serve a notice requiring a farmer to bring storage up to current standards if it believes there is a significant risk of pollution.
source_paragraphs: The Environment Agency can also serve a notice at any time requiring you to bring storage up to the current standards if it believes there's a significant risk of pollution.
explanation: Regulation 7(1) is the direct legal basis for the Agency's power to serve a notice requiring works or precautions on persons with custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil, accurately reflected by the guidance's statement about the Agency serving notices to bring storage up to standard where there is pollution risk.
law_proposition_text: The Agency may serve a notice on a person who has custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil, or is responsible for the silo, slurry storage system or fuel oil storage tank, in circumstances in which these Regulations apply, requiring that person to carry out works, or take precautions or other steps, specified in the notice.
law_name: The Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (England) Regulations 2010

page_title: Storing silage, slurry and agricultural fuel oil
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer must notify the Environment Agency at least 14 days before beginning construction of a new or substantially changed store for silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.
source_paragraphs:

page_title: Storing silage, slurry and agricultural fuel oil
guidance_proposition_text: A farmer must not place slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels or reception pits within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters without written agreement from the Environment Agency.
source_paragraphs: You must not put slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels or reception pits within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters without written agreement from the Environment Agency.
explanation: The law permits placement within 10 metres if the Agency agrees in writing that precautions taken are adequate to avoid significant pollution risk; the guidance states a blanket prohibition without written agreement, omitting the nuance that adequate precautions (not merely written agreement alone) are the operative condition. The guidance thus covers only part of what the law requires, presenting the rule as simpler than it is.
law_proposition_text: No part of a slurry storage tank or any effluent tank, channels, or reception pit may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which slurry could enter if it were to escape, unless precautions are taken that the Agency agrees in writing are adequate to avoid any significant risk of pollution of controlled waters.

explanation: The law requires the base of a slurry storage tank to be impermeable; the guidance states slurry tanks must be impermeable, which is consistent with this requirement (though the guidance may not separately distinguish 'base' from 'walls').

source_paragraphs: Slurry tanks, reception pits, pipes and channels must be impermeable and meet the anti-corrosion standards set in British Standard 5502-50:1993+A2:2010. They should last for at least 20 years with maintenance.

law_proposition_text: The slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit must be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for at least 20 years.

guidance_proposition_text: When calculating the required capacity of a steel or concrete slurry store, a minimum of 300 millimetres of freeboard must be included.
