source_paragraphs:
You must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on or between the following dates (closed periods):
from 15 September to 15 January on grassland
from 1 September to 15 January on tillage land
explanation: The neighbouring proposition explicitly covers the closed period prohibition for grassland (15 September–15 January), resolving the specific concern that other land types and their closed period dates were omitted from the guidance.
law_proposition_text: A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser on land during the closed period.

page_title: Using nitrogen fertilisers in nitrate vulnerable zones
guidance_proposition_text: If a land manager grows crops not listed in the closed-period exemptions table, they must have written advice from a FACTS-qualified adviser before spreading manufactured nitrogen fertilisers during the closed period.
source_paragraphs: If you grow crops that aren't listed in the table, you must have written advice from a FACTS-qualified adviser before you spread manufactured nitrogen fertilisers.
explanation: The regulation permits spreading on unlisted crops provided it follows written FACTS adviser advice; the guidance accurately restates this as an obligation to obtain such written advice before spreading — the permissive framing in law and the obligatory framing in guidance are substantively equivalent given that without the advice the activity is not permitted.
law_proposition_text: A person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during the closed period on a crop not specified in the table in paragraph (5), provided the spreading is in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser.

guidance_proposition_text: Limits on fertiliser use do not apply to land inside greenhouses, glasshouses and polytunnels where the land is enclosed for the whole calendar year.

If land is exposed to the open air at any time (for example, if you uncover a polytunnel) the limits apply for the whole of that year.
explanation: Regulation 9 exempts Part 4 from applying to nitrogen fertiliser on crops in a greenhouse, but the guidance extends this to glasshouses and polytunnels, adds a 'whole calendar year' enclosure condition, and speaks to 'limits on fertiliser use' generally rather than just Part 4 restrictions. The guidance sets a broader/higher bar than this single clause.
law_proposition_text: Part 4 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser on a crop growing in a greenhouse.

guidance_proposition_text: Limits on fertiliser use do not apply to land inside greenhouses, glasshouses and polytunnels where the land is enclosed for the whole calendar year.

guidance_proposition_text: A low-intensity farmer is one where at least 80% of their land is grassland, no more than 100kg of nitrogen per hectare per year is applied as organic manure, no more than 90kg of nitrogen per hectare per year is spread as manufactured fertiliser, and no organic manure is brought onto the holding.
source_paragraphs:
You're a low-intensity farmer if all of the following apply to you:
at least 80% of your land is grassland
you apply no more than 100kg of nitrogen per hectare per year as organic manure (including any nitrogen in manure deposited on the field by livestock)
you spread no more than 90kg of nitrogen per hectare per year as manufactured fertiliser
you don't bring any organic manure onto your holding

explanation: Regulation 31(1)(c-e) imposes a general record-keeping obligation on all occupiers who spread organic manure with no stated low-intensity exemption; the guidance claims low-intensity farmers are exempt, which goes beyond (and potentially conflicts with) what this provision says — but since the exemption may exist elsewhere in the instrument, GUIDANCE_BROADER is the more appropriate label under rule 4 rather than CONFLICTS.
law_proposition_text: The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the date, the method, and the type of organic manure spread.

guidance_proposition_text: Within 1 week of bringing livestock manure onto or sending it off their holding, a land manager must record the type and amount of manure and the date it was brought onto or sent off their holding.
source_paragraphs:
Within 1 week of bringing livestock manure (including poultry manure and slurry) onto your holding or sending it off, you must record:
the type and amount of manure and the date it was brought onto or sent off your holding
the total nitrogen content of any manure you send off or bring onto your holding
the name and address of the supplier or recipient of the manure
a contingency plan you'll follow if the manure isn't accepted by a recipient (for example, how you plan to store the manure)
explanation: This clause requires recording the date on which livestock manure was sent off a holding within one week, directly matching the date-recording element of the guidance for the sending-off scenario.
law_proposition_text: An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the date on which it was sent off the holding.
